SELENO v0.8 · CG-5 motor drive

Drive stress analysis

Linear static FEA of every printed part on the final assembly, in PLA and PETG, under motor, belt, pulley, connector and handling loads. It includes a check of each bolted joint.

Assembly
CG5_SelenoCompact_Motors_C8N.iam, with RA bracket v3 (STEP export 2026-11-10)
Date
2026-11-10
Parts
Frame, base plate, RA bracket, 2 RA straps, Dec bracket, Dec clamp cap, 2 Dec band caps
Solver
Quadratic tets, 770k + 587k DOF

Verdict

Motor brackets: pass in normal use

At full motor stall the RA bracket peaks at 5.8 MPa, a safety factor of at least 5.3. The Dec bracket peaks under 2 MPa. The belt pull moves either motor face by 0.1 mm or less.

RA bracket v3: knock margin fixed

v2 reached 30.1 MPa when the RA motor's back end took a 50 N knock (SF 1.4). v3 has a 6.5 mm plate and a filled-out corner, and peaks at 17.6 MPa: a safety factor of 3.0 along the layers and 2.1 across them.

Connector wall: fails a sideways cable snag

50 N pulled sideways at the end of a GX plug (90 mm out) puts 170 to 242 MPa into the 2 mm wall, which reaches its strength at about 8 to 12 N. A 20 N sideways pull on the DC plug also goes past its limit. Straight pull-outs hold, with SF 1.5 to 2.4 at 50 N.

Bolted joints: secure at low torque

Every joint holds with a large margin, provided the torque is kept low so the plastic under the heads and nuts doesn't creep. The one exception is the flat-bit M5s, which need washers.

Belt: don't over-tighten

At 40 N per span, the motor bearing sees about 64 N against a typical 28 N rating. At 15 N per span it is 24 N. A toothed belt needs pretension only to stop backlash; extra tension adds no holding power.

PLA or PETG: same stresses, choose on heat

The stresses are almost identical. PETG flexes about 1.5 times more, but it keeps its shape to about 68 °C, where PLA softens at about 55 °C. A mount left in a car or in the sun should be PETG.

What to change

  1. Take the cable snag off the connectors. Clip or strap each cable to the mount within about 100 mm of its plug, with a little slack, so a pull on the cable loads the mount and not the plug. On its own, a 4 mm wall would only bring the 50 N sideways case down to about yield, because stress scales with 1/thickness². Right-angle GX plugs would roughly halve the lever as well.
  2. Set the belts to about 15 N per span. Pressing the middle of a span with about 2 N (a 200 g weight) should move it about 1.5 to 2 mm. Over-tightening gains nothing: stall needs only 88 N of belt pull. It loads the motor bearings, the brass worm stubs and the brackets for no benefit.
  3. Use the torques in the joint table and add washers. M5 washers under the flat-bit screws give a 1.7 times higher clamp. Nyloc nuts fit the M3 (4.4 mm) and M4 (5.2 mm) pockets and stop the joints backing off as the plastic relaxes. Re-check the torque after a day.
  4. Done in RA bracket v3: a stiffer motor plate. A 1.5 mm pulley-side pad makes the plate 6.5 mm, keeping the slots and the centre hole. It clears the belt by 2 mm. The RA motor now uses 4x M3x10 screws. Print the plate flat so that bending runs along the layers.
  5. Done in RA bracket v3: the corner and the knife edge. The corner beside the +x motor slot is filled out. That removes the 2 mm ligament between the slot end and the plate edge, and gives bolt #4's head seat a solid wall where it used to graze the edge with a 0.1 mm lip.

For a safety factor of 2, the GX sockets can take about 4 N sideways at the plug end, and the DC socket about 8 N. Straight pull-outs hold, with SF 1.5 to 2.4 at 50 N.

J7 / GPIO header. The PCB hangs from the frame and the Pi sits on the base, so frame flex shifts one relative to the other. Even a 50 N GX16 snag moves them 0.09 mm apart in PLA and 0.14 mm in PETG. That is well inside what a 2.54 mm pin header absorbs. The motor loads move them by less than 0.01 mm.

Motor, belt and pulleys

Both axes use the same drive: GT2 16T on the motor, 40T on the 6 mm brass worm stub, a 158 mm belt at 50.4 mm centres, and a NEMA 17 42x38 at 1.5 A rated about 0.45 N·m holding torque.

Bolted joints

The bolts themselves are loaded to only a few percent of their proof load. The risk with printed parts is preload lost to creep, not breakage. That is why the torques are low and nyloc nuts are suggested. Above about 40 °C PLA relaxes much faster than PETG.

How it was modelled

Geometry and mesh

The parts were taken straight from the 2026-11-09 assembly STEP, in their assembled positions, and meshed with 10-node (quadratic) tets of 1 to 4.5 mm, finer round the connector holes and bolt seats. The solver is MKL Pardiso, with a residual of 1e-15.

Mesh check (run on bracket v2): re-meshing the RA bracket with elements about 35% larger moved the knock-case peak from 30.1 to 30.1 MPa (-0%), and the stall case from 9.5 to 9.6 MPa. The quoted peaks are within about 2% of the converged value.

Contacts and supports

Parts that touch are bonded with stiff springs. Every face touching the CG-5 is fixed: the dovetail (0.15 to 0.3 mm slide fit), the strap and band bores, the tab faces and the M5 heads. Each bolt is a steel spring from head seat to nut seat, and preload is checked by hand from the bearing pressure.

Materials

EνAlong layersAcross layersSoftens
PLA2.3 GPa0.3652.3 MPa40.5 MPa55 °C
PETG1.5 GPa0.3850.8 MPa42.8 MPa68 °C

Stiffness from Prusament data sheets; strengths from Polymaker PolyLite data sheets, so both materials come from the same test method. SF along layers = strength / von Mises; SF across layers = layer strength / largest tensile stress. The across-layer figure assumes the worst print orientation.

Load cases

  • Belt pretension: 15 N/span (recommended) and 40 N/span (over-tight), both sustained
  • Stall: 0.45 N·m holding torque with a 40 N/span belt: tight side 88 N, slack side 0. Both directions
  • Knock: 50 N on the motor's back end, worst of 24 sideways directions
  • 50 N push and pull along the motor axis
  • Motor weight 0.28 kg and the parts' own weight in every case

Limits

The model is linear and elastic. It does not include creep, impact, fatigue or temperature, so the creep and heat notes above come from rules of thumb. The CG-5 surfaces were modelled from photos and are treated as rigid. Bonded contact doesn't let joints open or slide; the joint table checks that they don't. Peaks within about 5 mm of a bolt seat and 0.6 mm of a fixed face are left out, because the model idealises those spots; the bearing check covers the bolt seats. The material values are typical data-sheet figures, and print settings shift them.

Built with gmsh, scikit-fem and MKL Pardiso. The scripts are in reports/fea_python/.
